concept_options.title: الحلقة التي لا تراها  —  The Loop You Never See
concept_options.hook: كتبتَ سطراً واحداً. هو اتخذ أربعين قراراً. هذه الحلقة التي دارت وأنت تنتظر.
concept_options.visual_approach: Diagram-led motion graphics: a three-node cycle (يقرأ / ينفّذ / يتحقّق) that physically rotates, with a file tree illuminating on 'read', a diff stamping in on 'act', and a test bar flipping red→green on 'verify'. Each rotation is faster than the last until it stops on a green frame. Pure vector — no generated imagery. Frame-stepped to ~12fps for the Vox stamped cadence; motion blur deliberately absent.
concept_options.target_audience: Arabic-speaking developers and builders who have already tried an AI coding tool and don't have a mental model for why it takes many steps
key_points: Claude Code runs three blending phases — gather context, take action, verify results — repeating until the task is done (official documentation)
Verification is half the loop: it runs the tests, reads the failure, fixes, runs again
You are inside the loop — you can interrupt at any point
Edits are snapshotted before they happen, so they are reversible independently of git
concept_options.core_message: ليست أمراً واحداً ينفَّذ — بل حلقة تدور، وأنت داخلها.
concept_options.cta: اسأله أن يشرح الحلقة على مشروعك أنت
concept_options.tone: Calm authority. Explanatory, not promotional. No hype adjectives.
grounded_in: data_point: three blending phases repeating until complete (primary — Claude Code docs)
data_point: snapshots before editing; Plan mode gates the loop
underserved_gap: nobody animates the loop; the verification half is never shown
audience_question: 'Why does it take so many steps?'
misconception: 'you describe it once and it comes out finished'
concept_options.why_this_works: This is the brief's clearest underserved gap: the loop is defined in primary documentation and is the single mechanism that explains every other behaviour, yet none of the five landscape entries animates it. It also answers two of the audience's top questions at once, and the cycle is the most animatable structure in the brief — rotation is motion that carries meaning rather than decoration.

concept_options.title: لم يقرأ مشروعك  —  It Never Read Your Code
concept_options.hook: لم يقرأ مشروعك أبداً. يبحث عن الملفات الأربعة التي يحتاجها، كما تفعل أنت.
concept_options.visual_approach: Annotated-UI with the Vox highlighter sweep: a dense file tree fills the vertical frame, a grep query sweeps across it like a marker, four files ignite in the accent yellow while hundreds stay near-black, then those four lift out and pour into a context-window bar that fills partway and stops. The myth is stamped on screen then struck through. Vector only; the file tree is generated as data, not as an image.
concept_options.target_audience: Arabic-speaking users who assume the model has memorized their repository and are confused when it misses context
key_points: There is no vector database and no embeddings — it does not index your codebase
It searches with grep and reads a handful of files, orchestrated by the model
This is why it can work across a whole project but still miss what you never pointed it at
Giving it direction beats giving it everything — 'delegate, don't dictate'
concept_options.core_message: لا يحفظ مشروعك — يبحث فيه. ولهذا يهمّ ما تشير إليه.
concept_options.cta: جرّب: أخبره أين المشكلة، لا كيف يحلّها
concept_options.tone: Corrective but generous. Never smug about the misconception.
grounded_in: data_point: no vector database, no embeddings, grep plus file reads
misconception: 'the model has memorized your repo'
audience_question: 'Does it actually read my whole project, or is it guessing?'
visual_reference: highlighter/marker sweep annotation over a held frame
concept_options.why_this_works: The most load-bearing misconception in the audience research, and the one that explains both the agent's reach and its blind spots. It maps one-to-one onto the Vox highlighter vocabulary — the marker sweep applied to a code tree instead of a map — which is the most recognisably 'Vox' moment available for a software topic. Caveat carried from research: the no-index claim is a secondary source corroborated by the official docs' description of search tooling, so on screen it is phrased as behaviour, not as an internal architecture claim.

concept_options.title: أسرع بالإحساس، أبطأ بالساعة  —  Felt Faster, Measured Slower
concept_options.hook: ستة عشر مطوّراً خبيراً أحسّوا أنهم أسرع بـ20%. الساعة قالت: أبطأ بـ19%.
concept_options.visual_approach: Chart-led motion graphics: two bars race up from a shared baseline — 'الإحساس' overshoots into the accent yellow while 'القياس' sinks below the line in near-black — held long enough to land, then annotated with the study's own caveat in small type. Supporting beat: a 44% acceptance ring. The most mechanically reliable thing to author in code and the most legible in a vertical frame.
concept_options.target_audience: Arabic-speaking developers already using these agents weekly who have a felt experience the data contradicts
key_points: In METR's randomized controlled trial, 16 experienced developers took 19% longer across 246 real tasks
They had predicted a 24% speed-up beforehand, and still believed they were 20% faster afterwards
They accepted fewer than 44% of the generated code, most saying it needed major changes
METR's own caveat: a point-in-time measurement, on codebases the developers knew deeply
concept_options.core_message: الإحساس بالسرعة ليس قياساً لها — والفرق هو حيث يذهب وقتك فعلاً.
concept_options.cta: قِس مرّة بنفسك قبل أن تحكم
concept_options.tone: Sober, non-triumphalist. Neither boosterish nor doom.
grounded_in: data_point: METR 19% slower, 20% believed faster, 24% predicted (primary, RCT)
data_point: fewer than 44% of AI code accepted without major changes
audience_question: 'Is it actually faster, or does it just feel faster?'
concept_options.why_this_works: The only genuinely counterintuitive number in the brief, and the only one from a randomized controlled trial rather than a vendor survey. Expectation-versus-reality as two diverging bars is the canonical Vox chart moment. Risk to weigh: it is the least flattering angle to the subject and the hardest to land honestly in 60 seconds — METR's caveat must survive into the script, which costs roughly a fifth of the word budget.

concept_options.title: ما قرّره وأنت لا تنظر  —  What It Decided While You Weren't Looking
concept_options.hook: «أضف تسجيل دخول.» فاختار قاعدة بياناتك، وقواعد جلساتك، ومكان أسرارك.
concept_options.visual_approach: Kinetic Arabic typography plus a progressive stack build: one short prompt line sits at the top of the frame, then silent decision chips stack beneath it one at a time — قاعدة البيانات، التحقّق، الجلسات، مفاتيح الأسرار — accelerating until they overflow the bottom of the frame, then the whole stack snaps into a single highlighted row: 'المراجعة مهمّتك'. Word-level Arabic reveals only, stepped cadence.
concept_options.target_audience: Arabic-speaking first-time builders who shipped something that worked and then could not fix it
key_points: A short prompt expands into decisions you never see — database setup, auth, session rules, where secrets live
A demo is not a production app; auth and data access are the easiest things to get silently wrong
This is why it works, then breaks after the next change
Review is the part that did not get automated
concept_options.core_message: الكود صار رخيصاً. المراجعة هي العمل الذي بقي لك.
concept_options.cta: اطلب منه أن يسرد ما قرّره قبل أن تقبل
concept_options.tone: Warm and non-judgemental. Speaking to someone who got burned, not scolding them.
grounded_in: audience_question: 'What is it deciding for me that I never see?'
pain_point: 'works, then breaks, and I cannot tell what changed'
misconception: 'if it compiles and runs, it is done'
landscape: vibe-coding failure catalogues name database setup and API keys as the unseen choices
concept_options.why_this_works: This is the audience's actual lived pain rather than a fact about the tool, and it has a natural narrative shape — one line in, an unfolding stack of consequences out. It is also the cheapest and most Arabic-native concept: it is carried almost entirely by typography, so the glyph-joining constraint costs nothing and the frame never fights the vertical crop. Weakness to weigh: it is the least mechanistic of the four, so the viewer learns a caution rather than a model.

selected_concept.rationale: AGENT RECOMMENDATION, PENDING USER CONFIRMATION — not yet a user choice. c1 ('the loop you never see') is recommended because it is the only concept grounded in a primary source for its central claim, it closes the brief's clearest underserved gap, it answers two of the audience's top questions in one structure, and a rotating cycle is the one shape where motion carries the meaning rather than decorating it. c2 is the strongest runner-up and the most recognisably Vox; c3 carries the best single number but the least flattering frame and an expensive caveat; c4 is the cheapest and most Arabic-native but teaches a caution rather than a model.

production_plan.playbook: custom: vox-ar-explainer (to be generated at scene_plan; no preset in styles/ matches the design read)

taste_profile.design_read: Arabic newsroom explainer for a sound-off vertical feed: stamped, evidential, and unhurried in the holds while sharp on the cuts. It should read as journalism about a tool, not as marketing for one — the authority comes from showing the mechanism, never from adjectives.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Near-black ink ground, one saturated accent used only on the thing being asserted, paper-white for type. Zero gradients, zero glow, zero rounded corners. Nothing is decorative — if an element is coloured, it is the claim.
taste_profile.layout_variation: Two scene families only: full-frame typographic assertion, and annotated object (tree, cycle, chart, stack) held in the vertical safe area with its label above it. Alternate between them so no two adjacent beats share a family.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: No AI reference stills needed or available — every element is authored as vector. Instead: one layout still exported per scene family before the full build, checked for Arabic shaping and safe-area fit at 1080×1920.
anti_patterns: Per-letter Arabic animation of any kind — breaks glyph joining
Smooth eased motion blur — the Vox read depends on stepped, blur-free motion
On-screen labels that merely repeat the narration line
Terminal/code-rain cliché as a stand-in for 'AI coding'
quality_gates: Freeze any frame: it must still read with the sound off
Every Arabic reveal is word-level (split on spaces only), direction verified under RTL
All type and charts inside the vertical safe area — ~270px top, ~670px bottom, ~65px sides
Latin tokens ('Claude Code', 'grep', 'METR') set dir=ltr in the Latin face
Could this video belong to any other topic with the title swapped? If yes, the direction failed
No Claude model performance numbers, prices, or digital specs anywhere on screen

stages.approach: Write in Vox board structure: one visual idea, one narration line, one non-redundant on-screen label per beat. 60s at Arabic narration pace targets ~130-150 words across ~12 beats. Latin product names kept LTR. METR's caveat budgeted into the word count if c3 is selected.

Lock the two scene families, the transition family (hard cut plus one directional whip per act break), per-scene animation mode, and the generated custom playbook. Timings left provisional until the narration audio exists, then calibrated to it.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: ElevenLabs Arabic narration (~$0.26, blocked on connector reconnect) vs piper_tts ar_JO-kareem local (free, available after a pip install) vs no narration at all (free, available now)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Hold for the ElevenLabs reconnect, as chosen. Arabic prosody is where cheap TTS fails most audibly, and a 60-second piece lives or dies on the voice.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: ElevenLabs: natural prosody, auditionable voices. Piper: intelligible but audibly synthetic, Jordanian accent, no voice choice. No narration: forces every idea through type, which suits a muted feed but loses the Vox narration-plus-label interplay that makes the board structure work.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Atelier authoring (hand-authored scenes, bespoke theme) vs templated authoring (stock cut-types and the existing chart stack)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Atelier. The guide defaults hero work to atelier, and a recognisable house style is precisely what templated stock scene-types cannot produce — they are frozen looks that reintroduce sameness.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Atelier costs materially more tokens and iteration and has no reusable creative components. Templated would be faster and cheaper but would make this look like every other OpenMontage video, which fails the taste profile's own last quality gate.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Zero paid visual assets (all vector, authored) vs AI-generated stills or clips for texture
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Zero paid visuals — and not merely because no provider is configured: flat authored vector IS the Vox vocabulary for a software topic. Generated imagery would actively fight the style.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: No photographic or archival texture, which real Vox uses heavily. For a code topic that vocabulary does not apply anyway — there is no archive of 'an agent reading a file tree'.

decisions.subject: Pipeline for a Vox-style 60s vertical Arabic explainer

options_considered.label: animation (motion graphics, diagram-led explainers, kinetic typography)
options_considered.reason: Vox style for a software topic is diagram, chart and type led — exactly this pipeline's remit, and its manifest recommends flat-motion-graphics playbooks.

options_considered.label: animated-explainer (fully AI-produced from topic)
options_considered.reason: Assumes generated narration plus generated visuals.
options_considered.rejected_because: Its asset path leans on image and video generation; 0 of 32 image and 0 of 36 video providers are configured, and generated imagery would fight the Vox vector vocabulary anyway.

options_considered.label: cinematic (mood-led, footage-first)
options_considered.reason: Built for supplied footage and trailers.
options_considered.rejected_because: No source footage and no mood-led brief; wrong grammar for an explainer.

decisions.reason: The brief is a diagram-and-type explainer with no footage and no generated imagery, which is the animation pipeline's core case.

decisions.subject: Composition runtime

options_considered.label: HyperFrames (HTML/CSS/GSAP → MP4)
options_considered.reason: The selector routes kinetic typography and HTML/GSAP-native motion here, and the registry's motion-graphics guidance points the same way. Arabic shaping and RTL are native browser text layout rather than something to reimplement, and the stepped blur-free Vox cadence is straightforward in CSS/GSAP.

options_considered.label: Remotion (React components → MP4)
options_considered.reason: Available after this session's dependency install. Owns word-level caption burn and the existing chart stack, and matches the user's existing tasmeem project, so patterns transfer.
options_considered.rejected_because: Recommended against, not rejected — the user decides. In atelier mode the existing chart stack is off-limits anyway, which removes Remotion's main advantage here, and React component authoring is more rigid than HTML/CSS for bespoke typographic motion.

options_considered.label: ffmpeg concat only
options_considered.reason: Available.
options_considered.rejected_because: No composition layer; cannot build animated diagrams, charts or type.

decisions.reason: Both runtimes are available, so the HARD RULE requires presenting both and waiting. Agent recommends HyperFrames for native Arabic/RTL text layout and HTML/GSAP-native stepped motion; Remotion is a legitimate pick, especially to reuse tasmeem patterns and word-level caption burn. Not written into production_plan until the user picks.

decisions.subject: Composition authoring mode

options_considered.label: Atelier — hand-authored scenes, one-off theme and motion
options_considered.reason: The guide defaults hero work to atelier, and the request is for a specific recognisable house style. Stock cut-types are frozen looks that reintroduce sameness, which fails the taste profile's own distinctness gate.

options_considered.label: Templated — stock cut.type scenes in the Explainer composition
options_considered.reason: Faster, cheaper, more reliable; right for batch output and drafts.
options_considered.rejected_because: Recommended against: a Vox look assembled from the shared scene catalogue would read as the catalogue, not as Vox. Costs the user the one thing they asked for.

decisions.reason: Agent recommends atelier and says plainly that it costs more tokens and iteration than templated, so the user opts in knowingly.
